name: BFS / DFS
summary: Traversal of a graph, grid or tree. BFS explores level by level with a queue, which gives shortest paths in unweighted graphs. DFS goes deep with a queue or stack, which finds components and paths.
signal: levels, shortest unweighted path, components, exploration, recursive traversal
mentalModel: BFS: spread out level by level. DFS: go deep, backtrack on dead ends.
recognitionRules: The structure is a grid, tree, or adjacency list.
You need the shortest number of steps in an unweighted graph.
You need connected components, cycles, or 'can we reach this node'.
The answer is the level, the depth, or the number of layers.
A brute force restarts exploration from every unvisited node (DFS).
template: visited.add(neighbour)      // mark on insert, not on pop
invariant: Nodes are processed in non-decreasing distance from the start, so the first time a node is reached its distance is minimal.
